goal: As a T&D specialist at a 350-person manufacturer, produce five linked deliverables: an OSHA SHP checklist gap analysis (PDF), a Q2 2025 schedule covering 180 employees in Safety Orientation with instructor-continuity handling and reinforcement sessions, a Kirkpatrick evaluation plan adapted for the floor with ERP diagnostics, an ROI workbook (cost-effectiveness, 200-employee Q2 budget, break-even), and an instructor capacity risk matrix.
delivered: OSHA_Gap_Analysis_Completed.pdf, Q2_2025_Training_Schedule.xlsx (8 sessions S-01..S-08 plus attendance register), Q2_Evaluation_Strategy.docx (Safety Orientation plan with a generic diagnostic module), Training_ROI_Analysis.xlsx (incident-based cost-effectiveness, Q2 budget, break-even) and Instructor_Risk_Matrix.xlsx (SPOF/expiry/coverage/action plan). The ROI workbook's computed cells are openpyxl formulas with no cached values, so they read as blank.
what_went_wrong: Most points were lost to design choices and omissions rather than missing data. The schedule has David Lee teaching a drill, not his own recertification (R0); safety cohorts are in TR-106 rather than equipped TR-105 (R7). The evaluation plan lacks pictorial scales (R1), ERP-specific diagnostic questions (R2) and a justified, shift-aware delayed-survey timeline (R8). ROI uses an incident/$25k-per-incident frame with no productivity-per-cost ranking, no Leadership NA note and no allocation percentages (R3). Training_ROI_Analysis.xlsx was saved with live formulas (=B7*C7, =SUM(...)) that were never recalculated, so the judge saw empty budget totals (R4). The risk matrix omits Max_Weekly_Hours and any demand-vs-capacity check, although the subagent reported Martinez 12h and Wilson 10h (R6).

failed_items.why: Backup coverage via Robert Johnson passed, but S-07 (2025-06-18) is an Emergency Response 'Continuity drill' with David Lee as instructor. No session schedules Lee's own recertification before 2025-07-15; it appears only as an Action Plan line in the risk matrix.

Plain language, verbal administration and shift-friendly timing are present, but the instruments use only numeric 1-5 / 1-4 Likert scales. There are no visual or pictorial rating aids for varying literacy.

The agent identified Software/ERP as lowest L3 (69.0%), but its 'diagnostic module' is generic barrier interviews and observation of 5 ERP transactions. It has no ERP-specific questions on system access, workflow fit, supervisor requirement, reference materials or practice opportunities.

Historical Cost Effectiveness lists L4 averages but computes only incident-based cost metrics (as uncached formulas). It never derives productivity-per-cost ROI, never ranks Equipment Operation highest, never notes Leadership L4 is NA, and gives no ROI-based allocation percentages.

Q2 Budget holds formulas (D7 '=B7*C7', G9 '=SUM(G7:G8)', sensitivity B14 '=A14*125') with no cached values, so totals render empty. The subagent had already computed Safety 200 = $25,000 and Quality $55,000. The sheet also has no optimal-allocation recommendation, so the item would still be at risk after recalculation (medium confidence).

Instructor_Risk_Matrix columns cover ID, specialization, expiry, days to expiry and coverage roles, but no Max_Weekly_Hours and no Q2 demand-hours estimate. Martinez's 12h cap and Wilson's lowest 10h cap are never flagged, though both came from the staged CSV and the subagent summary.

Equipment Operation is correctly in TR-103, but the three 60-person Safety Orientation cohorts are in TR-106 ('avoids TR-105 cap 40', portable PPE kit) instead of the PPE/first-aid-equipped TR-105. Software/ERP was not scheduled at all, which the prompt did not strictly require since ERP L3 was rising (medium confidence).

The delayed survey runs at day 30 and day 60, but the timing is not justified as time for on-the-job application. Distribution is a uniform day-30/60 send with day-3/7 reminders, not planned around shifts.

subagent_notes: One 'Analyze source data' subagent summarized every input accurately: program L3/L4 trends, QC decline, ERP lowest, all instructor caps and expiries, room equipment, and $25,000/$55,000 budget figures. The root used it for SPOF/expiry (R5 passed) but dropped its capacity-hours and budget-value details from the deliverables.
